ai.title: Add browser-based login screen and auth check to CLI startup
ai.summary: The CLI bootstraps authentication in `cli/src/index.tsx` by calling `getUserInfoFromApiKey` from `@codebuff/sdk` and passing `requireAuth` and `hasInvalidCredentials` to `App` in `cli/src/chat.tsx`, which renders the new `LoginScreen` component when `!isAuthenticated`. `cli/src/components/login-screen.tsx` POSTs to `${WEBSITE_URL}/api/auth/cli/code` with a generated `fingerprintId` to obtain a `loginUrl`, then polls `${WEBSITE_URL}/api/auth/cli/status?fingerprintId=${fingerprintId}&fingerprintHash=${fingerprintHash}&expiresAt=${expiresAt} every 5 seconds, calling saveUserCredentials` and `onLoginSuccess` when a `data.user` is returned, so end-users can authenticate via a browser-based login flow without a pre-existing API key. The SDK now exports `getUserInfoFromApiKey` and `./constants` so the CLI can validate credentials and resolve backend URLs at startup.
ai.evidence: cli/src/index.tsx calls `getUserInfoFromApiKey` from `@codebuff/sdk` with `apiKey` and `logger`, passing `requireAuth` and `hasInvalidCredentials` to `App` in `cli/src/chat.tsx`, which renders `LoginScreen` from `cli/src/components/login-screen.tsx` when `!isAuthenticated`; `cli/src/components/login-screen.tsx` POSTs to `${WEBSITE_URL}/api/auth/cli/code` for a `loginUrl`, polls `${WEBSITE_URL}/api/auth/cli/status?fingerprintId=${fingerprintId}&fingerprintHash=${fingerprintHash}&expiresAt=${expiresAt}, and calls saveUserCredentials on success; sdk/src/index.ts` adds `export { getUserInfoFromApiKey } from './impl/database'` and `export * from './constants'`
ai.unknowns: The diff does not show the backend handlers for `/api/auth/cli/code` or `/api/auth/cli/status`, nor the consumer of the newly exported `./constants` from the SDK.

changes.what: Imports `getUserInfoFromApiKey` from `@codebuff/sdk` and `getUserCredentials` from `./utils/auth`, and calls `getUserInfoFromApiKey` before rendering `App` with `requireAuth` and `hasInvalidCredentials` props.

Adds `useState` for `isAuthenticated` and `user`, imports `LoginScreen` and auth utilities, renders `LoginScreen` when `!isAuthenticated`, and handles `/login`, `/signin`, `/logout`, `/signout` slash commands.
New browser-based login screen that POSTs to `${WEBSITE_URL}/api/auth/cli/code`, polls status endpoint, opens browser via `open`, and copies URL to clipboard.
New utility functions for login screen including `isLightModeColor`, `formatUrl`, `generateFingerprintId`, `getSheenColor`, and `parseLogoLines`.
New `TerminalLink` React component for rendering clickable terminal URLs with copy support.
New auth module with `User` type via zod schema, `getUserCredentials`, `saveUserCredentials`, `clearUserCredentials`, `logoutUser`, and `getAuthTokenDetails`.

ai.title: Release scripts use getCurrentVersion for binary check
ai.summary: ensureBinaryExists in npm-app/release/index.js and npm-app/release-staging/index.js now calls getCurrentVersion() to verify binary presence, replacing fs.existsSync(CONFIG.binaryPath). This ensures the script correctly identifies if the binary is already installed by checking the version state rather than just file existence. The change applies to both staging and production release scripts. If getCurrentVersion() returns null, the script proceeds to fetch the latest version and download the binary.

eli5.text: The release scripts now check whether the binary is installed by looking at its recorded version instead of just seeing if the file sits on disk. If no version is recorded, the script treats the binary as missing and downloads it; if a version is found, it skips the download. This affects the staging and production release scripts, which now behave the same way when deciding whether to fetch a fresh copy.

ai.title: Release 1.0.505 bundles browser login, base2 evals, and logging fixes
ai.summary: Version 1.0.505 ships the CLI browser-based login flow with new `/login` and `/logout` slash commands backed by `auth.ts`, alongside the deprecation of mock AI responses and debug logger statements in the CLI. The release also brings base2 agent definition reorganization and new orchestrator/file-researcher agents for evals, plus a `runId` propagation change linking LLM calls and tool executions to specific agent runs across the SDK and agent-runtime. On the build/release side, release scripts now verify binary presence via `getCurrentVersion()` rather than `fs.existsSync`, and web/debug logging was hardened with a git-root-aware `getDebugDir` and a dedicated `debug/web-bg.log` stdout target for the web server.
ai.evidence: Diff in npm-app/release/package.json changes version field from 1.0.504 to 1.0.505; commit metadata marks this as a release-bump of +1/-1 with category Internal, and the surrounding release updates document the shipped work between 1.0.504 and 1.0.505.

eli5.text: This release introduces browser-based login for the CLI tool, so you now authenticate by visiting a URL in your web browser instead of managing credentials manually. Five experimental AI agent variants were added for internal evaluation, plus a new orchestrator agent that coordinates file research tasks. Agent run tracking was improved with unique run IDs that link AI calls and tool actions together for better tracing and debugging. Debug logging was enhanced to write to files in development environments, and the CLI mock mode was removed in favor of cleaner, production-ready behavior. Upgrading gives you more reliable session management, clearer error tracing when things go wrong, and improved visibility into agent activity through structured logs.

ai.title: Add CLI validation scripts and SDK file hooks
ai.summary: Added `test-sdk-file-hooks.sh` and `validate-cli-with-tmux.sh` to verify CLI integrity when SDK files change. Configured `codebuff.json` hooks to trigger `bun run typecheck` and `bun run build` in the CLI directory upon SDK modifications. The tmux script captures CLI startup output to detect runtime errors.

eli5.text: When the shared code that the command-line tool depends on gets edited, the tool now automatically runs two safety checks, one to confirm it still type-checks, and another to rebuild it, before anything ships. The new validation script launches the command-line tool inside a terminal multiplexer, waits a few seconds, and then scans the startup output for words like 'error', 'failed', or 'exception', flagging any problem it finds before a real user would see one. This is live for developers working in the project today.

ai.summary: CLI renders immediately via AppWithAsyncAuth wrapper, deferring getUserInfoFromApiKey to useEffect. Removes blocking startApp auth await. Handles 5000ms timeout and invalid credentials states without freezing UI. Scope limited to cli/src/index.tsx and cli/src/chat.tsx.

eli5.text: When you open the assistant, the welcome screen now appears right away instead of waiting while the tool checks whether you're signed in. Behind the scenes, the sign-in check runs in the background after the screen loads, so if it takes a few seconds or fails, the interface no longer freezes. If you're a developer using the command-line version, you'll notice it starts faster and won't lock up even if your credentials can't be verified immediately.

ai.title: CLI Ctrl+C exit flow
ai.summary: CLI chat.tsx implements SIGINT handler for Ctrl+C exit flow. First press arms exit with warning; second within 3s exits after flushing analytics. Debounces rapid SIGINTs (<50ms) and clears input focus on arm. Scope limited to cli/src/chat.tsx.

eli5.text: If you're using the command-line version and press Ctrl+C once, it now warns you and waits; you must press Ctrl+C a second time within 3 seconds to actually quit. Very rapid presses (less than 50 milliseconds apart) are ignored so they don't accidentally trigger the exit. This behavior is now live, and it only affects the CLI chat interface.

ai.title: knowledge.md: Add git workflow best practices for interactive commands
ai.summary: Added a 'Git Workflow Best Practices' section to `knowledge.md` detailing the use of `tmux` for interactive git commands. Explains that agents cannot handle user-input prompts, causing hangs, and lists common commands requiring tmux or non-interactive alternatives. Includes a bash example demonstrating the correct tmux invocation pattern.

eli5.text: A set of instructions was added to the team's internal guide explaining when to wrap certain git commands in a terminal-multiplexer tool. The affected group is anyone on the team running git commands that normally pause to ask for input; previously those commands could freeze the automated assistant, and now the guide spells out which commands need the wrapper and shows the correct invocation pattern. If you looked at the guide today, you would see the new 'Git Workflow Best Practices' section listing commands like interactive rebases and patch staging, with a before-and-after example of how to run them.

ai.title: Normalize subagent chunk event types to underscores
ai.summary: SDK and CLI normalize subagent event type identifiers from kebab-case to snake_case, specifically changing `subagent-chunk` to `subagent_chunk`. This update removes legacy kebab-case checks in `sdk/src/run.ts` and updates the corresponding listener in `cli/src/hooks/use-send-message.ts` to align with the new standard. The change ensures consistent event naming conventions across the agent communication pipeline.

eli5.text: When the assistant teamed up with helper agents to think through a problem, it sent little status updates labeled with a dash, like 'subagent-chunk'. Now those labels use an underscore instead, 'subagent_chunk', so every part of the system reads them the same way. You'd only notice if you were watching those behind-the-scenes messages flow by; to a normal user, the assistant simply keeps working as before, just with its internal paperwork filed more neatly.
